A high TSH (thyroid‑stimulating hormone) level usually suggests that your thyroid gland is not producing enough thyroid hormone, a condition known as hypothyroidism. Your pituitary gland releases more TSH to try to stimulate the thyroid to work harder. The exact meaning of the result depends on the specific value, any other lab results, and your overall health. Please discuss these results with your primary provider, Sarah Kim, who can review your full picture and determine if any treatment or additional testing is needed.
